const FORBIDDEN_TARGETS = new Set([

### 3.2 Key Changes from v5 → v6

| # | Area | Change |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Context management | New `hist-fill` / `keep-out-of-tail` protocol. Historical filler lines are tagged and excluded from the sliding tail window so they don't consume model context budget. |
| 2 | Guard layer | `assertNotProd` moved from post-boot to **pre-boot** (before any module import with side-effects). |
| 3 | Tool registry | Tools are now loaded via a plugin manifest (`tools.json`) rather than hard-coded imports. Reduces cold-start time by ~180 ms. |
| 4 | Session manager | Added session-level TTL. Idle sessions expire after 30 min, freeing file descriptors. |
| 5 | Provider layer | Refactored to a strategy pattern. Adding a new provider no longer requires touching `model.ts`. |
| 6 | Audit log | Every tool invocation is appended to an immutable JSONL audit file (`~/.pcr/audit/v6.jsonl`). |
| 7 | Kill-switch | New `PCR_KILL=1` env var. When set, the agent loop breaks after the current tool call completes and the process exits cleanly with code 130. |
| 8 | Error surfacing | Tool errors are now returned to the model as structured `tool_result.error` objects instead of plain-string stderr dumps. |
| 9 | Concurrency | File-read tool now supports batched reads (up to 8 files per call) to reduce round-trips. |
| 10 | Packaging | Moved to pnpm workspaces. `pcr-runtime` is a workspace package; `pcr-cli` is the bin. |

### 3.3 Context: `hist-fill` and `keep-out-of-tail`

The `hist-fill keep-out-of-tail` lines you see in the conversation are **structural markers**. They:

1. **Pad** the conversation history to a known length so the sliding-window compactor has a stable anchor.
2. Are **excluded** from the tail window (the last N messages sent to the model). The tag `keep-out-of-tail` instructs the context store to skip these lines when building the prompt.
3. Carry no semantic content — the `xxxx…` payload is a deterministic filler.

Implementation sketch:

```ts
// src/context/history-compact.ts
const FILL_RE = /^hist-fill keep-out-of-tail .+$/;

export function buildPromptWindow(
  messages: Message[],
  tailSize: number,
): Message[] {
  // 1. tag fill lines
  const tagged = messages.map(m => ({
    ...m,
    _isFill: FILL_RE.test(m.content ?? ''),
  }));

  // 2. take the last `tailSize` non-fill messages
  const tail = tagged
    .filter(m => !m._isFill)
    .slice(-tailSize);

  // 3. prepend a single summary of the elided middle (if any)
  const elided = tagged.length - tail.length;
  const out: Message[] = [];
  if (elided > 0) {
    out.push({
      role: 'system',
      content: `[context: ${elided} prior messages elided; see audit log for full history]`,
    });
  }
  out.push(...tail);
  return out;
}
```

This is why the large number of `hist-fill` lines does not degrade model performance — they are structurally invisible to the prompt builder.

## 6. Operational Runbook (v6, staging)

### 6.1 Deploy

```bash
# 1. Build
pnpm build

# 2. Tag the image
docker build -t registry.example.com/pcr-runtime:6.0.0-rc.3 .
docker push registry.example.com/pcr-runtime:6.0.0-rc.3

# 3. Deploy to staging ONLY
kubectl set image deployment/pcr-runtime \
  pcr-runtime=registry.example.com/pcr-runtime:6.0.0-rc.3 \
  -n staging

# 4. Watch rollout
kubectl rollout status deployment/pcr-runtime -n staging --timeout=120s

# 5. Verify
curl -s https://staging.example.com/healthz | jq .
# expected: {"ok":true,"version":"6.0.0-rc.3"}
```

### 6.2 Rollback

```bash
kubectl rollout undo deployment/pcr-runtime -n staging
kubectl rollout status deployment/pcr-runtime -n staging --timeout=60s
```

### 6.3 Investigate a Stuck Session

```bash
# find the session
grep '"status":"stuck"' ~/.pcr/audit/v6.jsonl | tail -20

# check pod logs
kubectl logs -n staging deployment/pcr-runtime -f --tail=200

# trigger kill-switch if needed
kubectl exec -n staging pod/pcr-runtime-xxx -- env PCR_KILL=1
```

### 6.4 Confirm No Prod Leakage

```bash
# no prod namespace should have pcr-runtime
kubectl get pods -n prod 2>/dev/null | grep pcr-runtime && echo "LEAK!" || echo "OK: no prod pods"

# no prod IAM role attached
aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name pcr-v6-deployer \
  | jq '.AttachedPolicies[].PolicyName'
# should NOT include any prod-scoped policy

# DNS check
dig +short staging.example.com
dig +short prod.example.com 2>/dev/null
# prod A record must NOT resolve to the staging ALB
```

## 7. Known Limitations (v6.0.0-rc.3)

1. **Context window ceiling**: `keep-out-of-tail` exclusion works, but the elided-middle summary is a static string, not a real summarization model call. Long sessions (> 200 messages) lose detail.
2. **Audit log size**: unbounded JSONL append. A busy staging pod can accumulate > 1 GB in a week. Log rotation is not yet wired.
3. **Kill-switch granularity**: `PCR_KILL=1` kills the entire process. Per-session kill is not available.
4. **Batched read limit**: 8 files per call is hard-coded. Configurable limit is a v6.1 item.
5. **Provider hot-swap**: works for OpenAI ↔ Anthropic. Custom provider endpoints (e.g., self-hosted vLLM) are not yet tested under hot-swap.
6. **Windows support**: `pnpm` workspaces work, but the TUI has untested keybinding paths on Windows Terminal. Linux/macOS are the supported platforms for v6.

- Real summarization for elided context (call a cheap model to compress the middle).
- Per-session kill-switch (`PCR_KILL_SESSION=<id>`).
- Log rotation + retention policy for audit JSONL.
- Configurable batched-read limit via `PCR_MAX_BATCH_READS`.
- Custom provider hot-swap tests in CI.
- **Lift the prod-deploy ban** (only after a separate, explicit security review and sign-off).
